easy.explanation: Tamar was David’s daughter and Absalom’s sister.
Jonadab was Amnon’s friend and was described as a very subtil man.
Jonadab advised Amnon to lie down and make himself sick.
easy.q: What did Amnon pretend to be?

medium.explanation: The passage says Amnon found it hard to do anything to Tamar because she was a virgin.
medium.q: Why did Amnon find it hard to do anything to Tamar?

answers: To keep Tamar away from Amnon
To create an opportunity for Tamar to come to him
To tell David about Amnon’s love
medium.explanation: Jonadab told Amnon to ask David to send Tamar to prepare food for him.
medium.q: What was the purpose of Jonadab’s advice?

answers: To be troubled and growing weaker
medium.explanation: Jonadab asked why Amnon was troubled and becoming weak from day to day.
medium.q: In the passage, what does “lean from day to day” mean?

answers: He suggested that David send Absalom
He made David think Amnon needed Tamar’s help
He asked David to punish Tamar
challenge.explanation: Jonadab advised Amnon to pretend to be sick so David would send Tamar to him.
challenge.q: How did Jonadab use David to advance Amnon’s plan?

answers: It was practical but helped a wicked plan
It was meant to settle the brothers’ dispute
It was intended to protect Tamar
challenge.explanation: Jonadab gave an effective plan, but it helped Amnon pursue a harmful and sinful purpose.
challenge.q: What can be concluded about Jonadab’s advice?

answers: His desire made him avoid Tamar
His desire helped him control himself
His desire was strong, but he needed a scheme to approach her
challenge.explanation: Amnon was consumed by his desire, yet he did not act until Jonadab gave him a deceptive plan.
challenge.q: What was the connection between Amnon’s desire and his inability to act?

easy.explanation: Tamar kneaded flour, made cakes, and baked them for Amnon.
easy.q: What did Tamar prepare for Amnon?

answers: Bring the food into the chamber
easy.explanation: Amnon told Tamar to bring the food into the chamber so he could eat from her hand.
easy.q: What did Amnon ask Tamar to do after she entered the room?

answers: Forced her and cast her out
easy.explanation: Amnon forced Tamar and then ordered his servant to put her out.
easy.q: What did Amnon do to Tamar?

answers: So he could be alone with Tamar
So they could prepare the feast
medium.explanation: Amnon ordered every man to leave, leaving him alone with Tamar.
medium.q: Why did Amnon ask everyone to leave him?

answers: That she did not know how to cook
That the act was folly in Israel and would bring shame
medium.explanation: Tamar pleaded with Amnon not to do such folly in Israel and warned of the shame it would cause.
medium.q: What did Tamar argue when Amnon approached her?

answers: A special robe worn by virgin daughters of the king
A garment worn only during mourning
medium.explanation: The passage says the king’s virgin daughters were apparelled in such robes.
medium.q: According to the passage, what was the garment of divers colours?

answers: From desire and false love to great hatred
challenge.explanation: After forcing Tamar, Amnon hated her with a hatred greater than the love he had claimed.
challenge.q: What change is described in Amnon’s attitude toward Tamar?

answers: She immediately fled from Absalom’s house
She put ashes on her head, tore her garment, and cried
challenge.explanation: Tamar showed her grief by putting ashes on her head, tearing her garment, and crying.
challenge.q: How did Tamar respond after she was cast out?

answers: Amnon’s cruelty and his change from false love to rejection
Amnon’s desire to repair his wrong
challenge.explanation: Amnon not only forced Tamar but also rejected and expelled her, showing his cruelty.
challenge.q: What does Tamar’s being cast out emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Tamar’s Grief and the Family’s Silence

answers: She put ashes on her head and cried
easy.explanation: Tamar put ashes on her head, tore her garment, and went on crying.
easy.q: What did Tamar do after she was cast out?

answers: To hold her peace and not regard the matter
easy.explanation: Absalom told Tamar to hold her peace because Amnon was her brother.
The passage says David was very wroth when he heard what had happened.
easy.q: How did David react when he heard?

answers: Because she had already forgiven Amnon
medium.explanation: Absalom specifically reminded Tamar that Amnon was her brother.
medium.q: Why did Absalom tell Tamar to remain silent?

answers: He spoke kindly and harshly to Amnon
He kept his hatred for Amnon in his heart
medium.explanation: Absalom spoke neither good nor bad to Amnon because he hated him.
medium.q: What did Absalom do after Tamar was assaulted?

medium.explanation: Tamar remained lonely and deeply sorrowful in Absalom’s house.
medium.q: In this context, what does “desolate” mean?

answers: Tamar expresses her pain, while Absalom and David do not openly act against Amnon
Absalom praises Amnon for his actions
challenge.explanation: Tamar cries openly, while Absalom tells her to be silent and David is only said to be angry.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the family’s response to Tamar’s suffering?

answers: He concealed hatred that he had not abandoned
He did not know what had happened
challenge.explanation: The text directly states that Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced Tamar.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Absalom’s silence toward Amnon?

answers: She quickly returned to normal life
She remained desolate in Absalom’s house
challenge.explanation: Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
challenge.q: How is Tamar’s condition described after the event?

paragraphs.title: The Invitation to the Shearing Feast

easy.explanation: The passage says that two full years had passed.
easy.q: How much time passed before Absalom’s shearing feast?

easy.explanation: Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
easy.q: Whom did Absalom invite to the feast?

easy.explanation: David first declined to go because he did not want to be chargeable to Absalom.
easy.q: Who did not initially want to go to the feast?

medium.explanation: Absalom specifically asked that his brother Amnon go with them.
medium.q: What did Absalom ask David concerning Amnon?

answers: He promised Amnon would not stay long
He said Tamar would attend the feast
medium.explanation: Absalom pressed David until he allowed Amnon and the king’s sons to go.
medium.q: How did Absalom get David to agree?

medium.explanation: The celebration took place when the sheep were being sheared.
medium.q: What does “sheepshearers” refer to in this passage?

answers: The event appears joyful, but Absalom still hates Amnon
challenge.explanation: The feast appears to be a family celebration, but Absalom continues to hate Amnon.
challenge.q: What creates tension between the invitation and what the reader knows?

answers: It allows Amnon to reach the place where the plan will be carried out
challenge.explanation: David’s agreement places Amnon at the feast where Absalom’s plan will unfold.
challenge.q: Why is David’s agreement to send Amnon important to the plot?

answers: He created a broad family event that could conceal his intention
He did not want Amnon to come
challenge.explanation: The large invitation made the event appear to be an ordinary family celebration.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Absalom’s invitation to all the king’s sons?

easy.explanation: Absalom commanded his servants to smite and kill Amnon.
easy.q: Whom did Absalom command his servants to kill?

easy.explanation: Absalom fled to Talmai, king of Geshur.
The passage says Absalom was in Geshur for three years.
easy.q: How long did Absalom remain in Geshur?

answers: That all the king’s sons had been killed
That the feast hall had burned
medium.explanation: David was first told that Absalom had slain all the king’s sons.
medium.q: What was the first report David received?

answers: Jonadab and the king’s sons who arrived
medium.explanation: Jonadab explained that Amnon alone was dead, and then the king’s sons arrived.
Tearing one’s garments and lying on the earth were expressions of intense mourning.
medium.q: What did David’s tearing of his garments express?

answers: His mourning for Amnon lessened, while his longing for Absalom grew
He forgot both Amnon and Absalom
He began to hate the king’s sons
challenge.explanation: David was comforted concerning Amnon, but his soul longed to go to Absalom.
challenge.q: How did David’s feelings change over time?

answers: The event caused panic and mourning before the truth was known
They already knew that only Amnon had died
challenge.explanation: The first report said all the king’s sons were dead, causing David and his servants to mourn before the truth was revealed.
challenge.q: What does the false report reveal about David and the king’s sons?

answers: Absalom fled after ordering Amnon’s murder
David sent Absalom to Geshur because of the feast
challenge.explanation: After ordering Amnon’s death, Absalom fled and went to Geshur.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Amnon’s murder and Absalom’s flight?
